rationale: This is essentially the mechanical union of two archive entries ("Balanced Intangible DuPont Value" and the oancf/gross-profit leg of "Cash-Backed Gross-to-Cash Funnel") bolted onto the same che/market-cap value leg, and stacking a third MIN rank mostly narrows the binding constraint and coverage rather than testing a new economic mechanism.

Adjusted margin times total-capital turnover is algebraically the same return-on-total-capital already used as the quality leg of the archived "Innovation Profit Surprise Value" (ls_talpha 3.84), so replacing the product with a MIN of its two components is a cosmetic reparameterization of an already-evaluated signal.

The added gross-profit-to-cash hurdle is economically distinct from the accrual-based payoff legs, but the construction is still "best archive signal (Multi-Year Physical Payoff Balance, ls_talpha 4.92) plus one more MIN leg," which risks coverage loss and unstable portfolio composition without a diagnosed reason why the existing signal fails.

The valuation leg is copied verbatim from "Innovation-Funding Residual Cash Value" and the two quality legs verbatim from "Total-Capital Payoff Balance," making this a recombination of already-evaluated components rather than a new mechanism, and the two intangible-capital quality terms are near-duplicates (level and 3-year change of the same adjusted-profit-to-capital construct).

The pairing is new — budgeted-liquidity value with a gross-profit-on-total-capital plus gross-to-cash two-stage funnel, and GP/(at + R&D stock) is a quality term not yet tested — though the archive already suggests subtracting the R&D budget weakens the cash-yield leg (ls_alpha 0.024 vs 0.060), so it may well come in below the existing plain-cash funnel.

GP/at times (oibdp−dp)/GP is an exact identity for post-depreciation ROA, which is precisely the quality leg of the archived "Maintenance-Adjusted Cash Franchise," so this is a DuPont re-slicing of the same quantity paired with an identical value leg rather than a substantively different hypothesis.
